'''Catherine Helen O'Neil''' (born 1972) is an American mathematician, data scientist, and author.  She is the author of the ''New York Times'' best-seller ''[[Weapons of Math Destruction]]'', and opinion columns in [[Bloomberg View]].   O'Neil was active in the [[Occupy movement|Occupy]] movement.<ref name="pbsInterview"/>

== Education and career ==
O'Neil attended [[UC Berkeley]] as an undergraduate,<ref name=pbsInterview>{{cite web|title=PBS Interview|website=[[PBS]] |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/oral-history/financial-crisis/cathy-oneil/|access-date=25 July 2013}}</ref> received a [[Ph.D.]] in [[mathematics]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1999,<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=38230 Catherine Helen O'Neil], ''[[Mathematics Genealogy]]''.</ref><ref name=2016LAT /> and afterward held positions in the mathematics departments of [[MIT]] and [[Barnard College]].<ref name="2017Politico">{{cite web |title=#49 Cathy O'Neil - POLITICO 50 2017 |url=https://www.politico.com/interactives/2017/politico50/cathy-oneil/ |website=POLITICO}}</ref> She left academia in 2007, and worked for four years in the finance industry.<ref name=econ>{{cite web|title=Library of Economics and Liberty interview|url=http://www.econtalk.org/archives/2013/02/cathy_oneil_on.html|access-date=25 July 2013}}</ref> She worked as an analyst at [[D. E. Shaw & Co.]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://time.com/4471451/cathy-oneil-math-destruction/ |title=This Mathematician Says Big Data Is Causing a 'Silent Financial Crisis' |date=August 29, 2016 |work=Time |last=Faroohar |first=Rana}}</ref> After becoming disenchanted with the world of finance, O'Neil became involved with the [[Occupy Wall Street]] movement,<ref name="2016CNNMoney">{{cite web |last1=Rawlins |first1=Aimee |title=Math is racist: How data is driving inequality |url=https://money.cnn.com/2016/09/06/technology/weapons-of-math-destruction/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160906231334/http://money.cnn.com/2016/09/06/technology/weapons-of-math-destruction/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 6, 2016 |website=CNNMoney |access-date=28 February 2021 |date=6 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="pbsInterview"/> participating in its Alternative Banking Group.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2011/12/ows-alternative-banking|publisher=[[Mother Jones magazine]]|title=Meet the Financial Wizards Working With Occupy Wall Street|author=Josh Harkinson|date=Dec 13, 2011}}</ref>

O'Neil operates the blog mathbabe.org and is a contributor to Bloomberg View.<ref name="2020WPLive">{{cite news |last1=Washington Post Live |title=The Future of Work with Humu CEO Laszlo Bock & ORCAA Founder Cathy O'Neil |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/washington-post-live/2020/11/10/future-work/ |access-date=28 February 2021 |newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref><ref name=2016Guardian>{{cite news |last1=Chalabi |first1=Mona |title=Weapons of Math Destruction: Cathy O'Neil adds up the damage of algorithms |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2016/oct/27/cathy-oneil-weapons-of-math-destruction-algorithms-big-data |access-date=28 February 2021 |work=The Guardian |date=27 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Pazzanese |first1=Christina |title=Don't trust that algorithm |url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2016/10/dont-trust-that-algorithm/ |website=Harvard Gazette |date=13 October 2016}}</ref>

Her first book, ''Doing Data Science'', was written with Rachel Schutt and published in 2013.<ref name=2016Guardian /> In 2016, her second book, ''Weapons of Math Destruction'', was published, long-listed for the [[National Book Award for Nonfiction]]<ref>{{citation|url=http://nationalbook.org/nba2016_nf_oneil-weapons-of-math-destruction.html|publisher=[[National Book Foundation]]|title=2016 National Book Award Longlist, Nonfiction}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.newyorker.com/books/page-turner/the-national-book-awards-nonfiction-longlist|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]|title=The National Book Awards Longlist: Nonfiction|date=September 14, 2016}}</ref> and became a ''New York Times'' best-seller.<ref name=2017Politico /> A third book, ''The Shame Machine: Who Profits in the New Age of Humiliation'', was published in March 2022.

She is the founder of O'Neil Risk Consulting & Algorithmic Auditing (ORCAA), an algorithmic auditing company<ref name="2016LAT">{{cite web |last1=Zhang |first1=Christine |title=Q&A: Cathy O'Neil, author of 'Weapons of Math Destruction,' on the dark side of big data |url=https://www.latimes.com/books/jacketcopy/la-ca-jc-cathy-oneil-20161229-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=28 February 2021 |date=30 December 2016}}</ref><ref name="2018Wired">{{cite magazine |last1=Hempel |first1=Jessi |title=Want to Prove Your Business Is Fair? Audit Your Algorithm |url=https://www.wired.com/story/want-to-prove-your-business-is-fair-audit-your-algorithm/ |magazine=Wired |access-date=28 February 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref> and is on the board of the nonprofit ORCAA Collaborative Expert Assistance Network (OCEAN).

== Awards ==
In 1993 O'Neil was awarded the [[Alice T. Schafer Prize]] from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] and in 2019 she won the [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA]]'s [[Euler Book Prize]] for her book ''Weapons of Math Destruction''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gallian|first=Joseph A.|date=2019-06-01|title=The First Twenty-Five Winners of the AWM Alice T. Schafer Prize|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=66|issue=6|pages=1|doi=10.1090/noti1892|issn=0002-9920|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
O'Neil lives in Massachusetts and has three sons.<ref name=mathbabeAbout>{{cite web|url=http://mathbabe.org/about/|access-date=30 September 2021|title=mathbabe.org about page|date=11 June 2011 }}</ref><ref name="harvard-kennedy-school">{{cite web |url=https://www.belfercenter.org/person/cathy-oneil#!person-bio |access-date=23 July 2023 |title=Kennedy School bio|date=3 August 2022 }}</ref>

==Bibliography==
* With Rachel Schutt, ''Doing Data Science: Straight Talk from the Frontline'' (O'Reilly 2013, {{ISBN|1449358659}}).
* ''On Being a Data Skeptic'' (O'Reilly Media 2013, {{ISBN|1491947233}}).  
* ''[[Weapons of Math Destruction]]'' (Crown 2016, {{ISBN|0553418815}}).
* ''The Shame Machine: Who Profits in the New Age of Humiliation'' (Crown 2022, {{ISBN|1984825453}}).
